# morph

> The public API package for the **Morph** UI framework — a compiler-driven
> runtime for building native desktop apps with JSX and TypeScript.

Morph is a **compile-time** framework. All API calls below are statically
analyzed by the Morph compiler and compiled into native code at build time.
This package exists so that Node.js, bundlers, editors, and TypeScript can
resolve `import ... from "morph"` — it is installed automatically when you
scaffold a project (e.g. `morph create`).

## Installation

```bash
npm install morph
# or
pnpm add morph
# or
yarn add morph
```

## Quick start

```tsx
import { CSS, morphState, morphEffect } from "morph";

// Load a stylesheet (local path or URL) — handled at build time.
CSS.load("./style.css");
CSS.load("https://cdn.example.com/theme.css");

export const windowConfig = {
  title: "Morph App",
  width: 800,
  height: 600,
};

export default function App() {
  const [count, setCount] = morphState(0);

  morphEffect(() => {
    console.log(`Count changed to: ${count}`);
  }, [count]);

  return (
    <body>
      <button onClick={() => setCount((prev) => prev + 1)}>
        Clicked {count} times
      </button>
    </body>
  );
}
```

## API

### `CSS.load(path)`

Loads a stylesheet into the application at build time.

| Parameter | Type     | Description                                             |
| --------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`    | `string` | Local file path (e.g. `"./style.css"`) or URL (e.g. `"https://…/theme.css"`) |

**Returns:** `void`

```tsx
import { CSS } from "morph";
CSS.load("./style.css");
```

### `morphState<S>(initialState)`

Creates a reactive state variable. Returns a tuple of the current state and a
dispatcher, mirroring React's `useState`. Morph tracks the variable and
re-renders the component automatically when it changes.

| Parameter      | Type             | Description                              |
| -------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `initialState` | `S \| () => S`   | Initial value, or lazy initializer.      |

**Returns:** `[S, (value: S | ((prev: S) => S)) => void]`

```tsx
const [count, setCount] = morphState(0);
setCount(count + 1);            // direct value
setCount((prev) => prev + 1);   // updater function
```

### `morphEffect(effect, deps?)`

Registers a side-effect that runs after the component renders. Runs once on
mount, then again whenever any dependency in `deps` changes. Return a cleanup
function to run before re-execution and on unmount.

| Parameter | Type                                | Description                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `effect`  | `() => void \| (() => void)`        | Side-effect; may return a cleanup function.  |
| `deps`    | `readonly any[]` (optional)         | Dependency list. Omit to run after every render. |

**Returns:** `void`

```tsx
morphEffect(() => {
  console.log(`Count changed to: ${count}`);
}, [count]);
```

### `windowConfig` (special export)

Exporting a `windowConfig` object from your entry file configures the native
application window. Equivalent to the `window` key in `morph.config.json`.

| Property | Type     | Description                              |
| -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `title`  | `string` | Window title shown in the title bar.     |
| `width`  | `number` | Window width in CSS pixels.              |
| `height` | `number` | Window height in CSS pixels.             |
| `modal`  | `boolean` (optional) | Window is modal, defaults to `false`. |

```tsx
export const windowConfig = {
  title: "Morph Installer",
  width: 700,
  height: 520,
};
```

### Global types

| Type                      | Description                                        |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `DispatchEffect<A>`       | Dispatches a state update, returning `void`.       |
| `SetStateAction<S>`       | A value, or updater function of the previous state.|
| `JSX.IntrinsicElements`   | Global JSX element registry for `.mx` / `.tsx`.    |

## TypeScript

The package ships its own type declarations (`index.d.ts`) and is
`sideEffects`-free. `"*.css"` module imports are declared so stylesheet imports
type-check out of the box.
